subject: Return code for functions that would otherwise be void?

messages.author: 49e107cb0f8a3d27
messages.subject: Return code for functions that would otherwise be void?
parts:
I'm refactoring some of the ADVI code. A few of the functions are currently void, in which they update a referenced vector. Occasionally the updating fails, and I want to know this so I can write something like "if update fails, then do something" in another function.

What's the correct Stan convention for the return value of this function. bool? (true if okay; false if failure) stan service error codes? (https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/blob/feature/advi-adapt-eta/src/stan/services/error_codes.hpp) I suspect the latter but I haven't seen it used very much in other Stan algorithms.

Dustin

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Return code for functions that would otherwise be void?
parts:
Neither. The right thing to do if something doesn't work is to
throw an exception, then let the first component in which it's
nested that can resolve the exception resolve it. That's why we
have lots of exceptions and exception types, but no error codes
anywhere. The basic pattern in a local context is this:

try {
do update;
} catch (const error_t& e) {
do something else;
}

where error_t is the error you know how to catch and resolve. But
what often happens is that a function just throws and something
non-local cleans up. That's what happens for arithmetic errors in
log prob or gradient evals --- they cause a failure which gets caught
by either the sampling or optimization algorithm.

BUT, if that "something else" is common and not really a "failure",
then you want to use a boolean, because there's no "error" to report
with a code.

- Bob
